To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
some Fusarium species, particularly F. moniliforme, are capable of producing a red color in turkey muscle, which is a major finding that may have a significant economic impact on the industry.
feeding of culture materials from some Fusarium species increased the redness (redder discoloration) of turkey breast muscle.
feeding experimentally moldy corn or rice to turkey poults resulted in increased redness in turkey muscle without obvious hemorrhages in the internal organs or in the musculure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the screening for toxigenic fungi, which could be responsible for the increased redness of turkey meat.
screening for toxigenic fungi in feed and feed ingredients.
the identification and characterization of mycotoxins produced by fungi isolated from corn and turkey feeds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increased redness of turkey muscle is caused by the culture materials of some Fusarium spp. and not by the mycotoxins of Fusarium spp.
Fusarium monilformme (M-1326) is a potential pathogen of the turkeys.
Fusarium monilorme M-1325, which is a common corn pathogen, can be a potential mycotoxin-producing fungus in corn and that it can cause increased redness in turkey muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fusarium species, which produce a wide array of toxins in corn and rice, can be a potential hazard to turkeys.
some fusarial isolates are toxigenic, but the toxic metabolites are not yet known.
Fusarium species were not found to produce mycotoxin(s) that could be responsible for the redness in turkey muscle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of culture materials of toxigenic Fusaria, Penicillia, and Aspergilus should be avoided in feeding trials.
Fusarium culture materials can cause reddening in the muscle tissue, which is an undesirable quality of fresh turkey meat.
culture materials of F. moniliforme M-1325 should not be used as feed ingredients.
